title: CORE FX
summary: Core's effects in one window: saturation, reverb, delay, modulation and lo-fi, each fed only by the parts of the spectrum you choose.
steps: Add CORE FX to a track from the Effects menu, or pick a preset for your style.

Each module (Saturate, Reverb, Delay, Modulate, Lo-fi) has its own colour. Turn it on and draw where it listens: drag a region on the spectrum, its height is how much of that band goes into the effect.
Set the module's Type and its two knobs. Return is how loud the effect comes back; Fit keeps what comes back near the frequencies that went in.
Amount turns every effect up or down at once: at 0 you hear the dry sound only. FX Only drops the dry sound, for an FX bus.
Solo a module to hear only what it adds. The limiter at the end keeps the peaks under control.

examples.title: A dark room for a bass top
examples.text: Only the top of the bass goes into a short dark room: the low end stays dry and tight.

examples.title: A lead that spirals
examples.text: Each echo climbs in pitch: the lead spirals out of tune behind itself.

examples.title: Moving hats
examples.text: A flanger on the hats only, moving with the tempo.

examples.title: A tail that shines
examples.text: The reverb tail rises an octave and glows: for slow leads and pads.

styles.why: Long reverbs and slow delays are part of the sound: send a lot, from wide regions.
Delays in 3/16 and soft halls on leads and pads, the low end kept dry.
Short dark rooms, spirals and drive on the mids, so the track keeps its drive.
Very short rooms and 1/16 delays on small regions: only to glue the sounds together.
